To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) for a multi-system database environment, the function request shipping (FRS) approach is more scalable than the data sharing (DS) approach in that it allows more users to be supported with the same hardware; and (2) the FRS approach is also more robust in that the system can be partitioned to achieve a higher degree of availability and a better load balance.

the function shipping approach has a lower response time than the data sharing approach for a wide range of workloads, that the function shipping and the data sharing approaches can be compared on the basis of a simple metric called the remote function ratio, that the function request shipping and data sharing multi-system approaches are complementary and that the function shipping multi-system database system can provide the same performance as the data sharing system if the remote function ratio is kept small enough.
1) The function shipping approach can achieve a substantial reduction in remote function calls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of multi-system database systems that use function request shipping to support a shared database.
the design and analysis of the multi-system function shipping approach.
issues of partitioning, routing, and system performance of multi-system database management systems with function request shipping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
function request shipping can be used as a practical alternative to data sharing, with performance that is comparable to data sharing, for a wide range of applications.
the function shipping approach is a viable alternative to the data sharing approach for large multi-system database systems.
the function shipping approach can provide substantial performance improvements over the data sharing approach in many applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
function shipping is a viable approach to multi-system database management.
the multi-system function request approach is feasible, but it has a higher overhead than a data sharing approach.
the function shipping approach can be made to perform well, but it is not as efficient as a well-designed data sharing approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the function shipping approach can achieve performance close to data sharing, with the added advantage of being more flexible in the face of changes in the workload.
function shipping has the potential to significantly reduce the number of remote function calls and the number of mirror transaction setups, as compared with the data-sharing approach.
, for large multi-system database applications, a function shipping approach is a viable alternative to the data sharing approach, and can provide significant performance improvements.
